zebralogic.title: Enforce uniqueness across each attribute category
zebralogic.principle: Each value in a category must appear exactly once across all houses; duplicate assignments violate the puzzle constraints.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: Whenever assigning values to houses, ensure no two houses share the same value within that attribute category.
zebralogic.example: Assigning the same car model to two different houses.

zebralogic.title: Preserve original case of attribute values
zebralogic.principle: Copy attribute values verbatim as they appear in the problem statement, preserving spelling and case.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: When outputting the final solution, ensure each attribute value matches exactly the case and spelling given in the puzzle.
zebralogic.example: Changing 'Swede' to 'swede' or misspelling 'BMW 3 Series' as 'BMW 3Series'.

zebralogic.title: Bidirectional equivalence for name‑attribute clues
zebralogic.principle: If a clue links a specific name to an attribute, enforce both directions: the name must have that attribute, and that attribute must belong to that name.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: When processing clues that associate a name with a value (e.g., 'Alice is British').
zebralogic.example: Assigning British nationality to Alice but allowing another person also to be British.

zebralogic.title: Bidirectional equivalence for attribute‑attribute clues
zebralogic.principle: When a clue states that two non‑name attributes belong to the same house, enforce that they co‑occur in the same house and that each appears only there.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: When processing clues linking two attributes (e.g., 'The person who owns a Honda Civic is short').
zebralogic.example: Assigning the Honda Civic to one house and short height to another house.

zebralogic.title: Apply direct placement constraints
zebralogic.principle: If a clue explicitly places an attribute in a specific house number, enforce that placement and propagate constraints accordingly.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: When a clue mentions a specific house number (e.g., 'The Ford F-150 is in the fifth house').
zebralogic.example: Placing the Ford F-150 in a house other than the fifth.

zebralogic.title: Output solution JSON with exact schema and no extra text
zebralogic.principle: Emit only the JSON object with top‑level keys 'reasoning' and 'solution' and the required table; any extra text or stray characters cause parsing errors.
zebralogic.example: Including explanatory text before the JSON.

zebralogic.title: Chain adjacency clues into consecutive blocks
zebralogic.principle: When multiple adjacency clues share a common intermediate attribute, treat them as a chain to form a consecutive block of houses in the specified order.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: When processing several adjacency clues that involve overlapping houses (e.g., A left of B and B left of C).
zebralogic.example: Failing to enforce that A, B, C must occupy three consecutive houses in that order.

zebralogic.title: Interpret ordering and adjacency clues correctly (including N houses between)
zebralogic.principle: When a clue uses terms like 'directly left of', 'directly right of', 'next to', 'somewhere left of', 'somewhere right of', or 'N houses between', enforce the exact positional relationship: adjacency for 'directly' and 'next to', inequality for 'somewhere', and exactly N houses separating for 'N houses between' (distance = N+1).
zebralogic.when_to_apply: Whenever processing a clue that describes relative positions of two houses.
zebralogic.example: Treating 'There are two houses between A and B' as A and B being two positions apart instead of three.

zebralogic.title: Chain equivalence clues across multiple attributes
zebralogic.principle: If multiple clues each link a pair of attributes, combine them transitively so that all linked attributes are assigned to the same house (e.g., Car=Honda Civic ↔ Height=short and Height=short ↔ Birthday=March imply Car=Honda Civic, Height=short, Birthday=March belong together).
zebralogic.when_to_apply: When you have two or more equivalence clues that share a common attribute, propagate the equivalence to bind all involved attributes to the same house.
zebralogic.example: Missing that the short person drives a Honda Civic and also has a March birthday, leading to assigning them to different houses.

zebralogic.description: Interpreting 'N houses between' as distance N
zebralogic.why_it_happens: The model confuses the phrase with a simple distance rather than counting the houses separating them.
zebralogic.how_to_avoid: Remember that 'N houses between' requires exactly N houses in between, so the positional distance is N+1.

zebralogic.description: Ignoring equivalence clues that bind two attributes to the same house
zebralogic.why_it_happens: The model treats each attribute independently and does not propagate the equivalence.
zebralogic.how_to_avoid: When a clue links two attributes, record a bidirectional equivalence and ensure they are assigned together.

zebralogic.why_it_happens: The model does not keep a global record of used values for each category.
zebralogic.how_to_avoid: Maintain a set of used values per attribute category and forbid duplicates.

zebralogic.description: Altering attribute values (spelling/casing) instead of copying them verbatim
zebralogic.why_it_happens: The model normalizes text for readability, forgetting the exact required format.
zebralogic.how_to_avoid: Copy attribute strings exactly as they appear in the puzzle.

zebralogic.description: Including extra explanatory text or stray characters outside the required JSON solution
zebralogic.why_it_happens: The model tries to explain its reasoning in the final output.
zebralogic.how_to_avoid: Output only the JSON object with the required keys.

zebralogic.description: Misinterpreting adjacency clues (e.g., treating “directly left of” as non‑adjacent or ignoring direction)
zebralogic.why_it_happens: The model interprets 'left of' as a generic ordering rather than adjacency.
zebralogic.how_to_avoid: When a clue uses 'directly' or 'next to', enforce adjacency with the correct orientation.
